disease_region_alignment_definition.STRONG: The dominant/high-intensity Grad-CAM region substantially overlaps the visible disease symptom region.
disease_region_alignment_definition.PARTIAL: Attention overlaps the visible symptom region but substantial attention is also directed elsewhere.
disease_region_alignment_definition.WEAK: Only a small portion of attention overlaps visible disease symptoms.
disease_region_alignment_definition.NONE: Visible symptoms are present but the dominant attention does not overlap them.
disease_region_alignment_definition.NOT_APPLICABLE: Used when disease-region alignment is not meaningful, for example a visually healthy case.
disease_region_alignment_definition.UNCERTAIN: Image/CAM does not permit reliable judgement.

background_bias_definition.NONE: Attention is essentially confined to leaf or relevant plant tissue.
background_bias_definition.MINOR: Small background attention exists but the dominant region remains leaf/symptom related.
background_bias_definition.MODERATE: Meaningful attention is split between leaf and background.
background_bias_definition.DOMINANT: The strongest attention is primarily outside relevant leaf/plant tissue.
background_bias_definition.UNCERTAIN: Background-bias strength cannot be reliably determined.

attention_semantic_region_definition.SYMPTOM_REGION: Dominant attention lies on visible disease symptoms.
attention_semantic_region_definition.NON_SYMPTOM_LEAF: Dominant attention lies on leaf tissue without obvious disease symptoms.
attention_semantic_region_definition.LEAF_AND_BACKGROUND: Substantial attention covers both plant tissue and image background.
attention_semantic_region_definition.BACKGROUND: Dominant attention is outside relevant plant tissue.
attention_semantic_region_definition.NON_LEAF_OBJECT: Dominant attention is on another visible object rather than relevant leaf tissue.
attention_semantic_region_definition.DIFFUSE_UNCLEAR: Attention is broad/diffuse and cannot be assigned to a single meaningful semantic region.
attention_semantic_region_definition.UNCERTAIN: Reliable semantic localization is not possible.

annotation_unit_policy.correct_case_primary_cam: Primary predicted-class CAM is also the correct-class CAM.
annotation_unit_policy.wrong_case_primary_cam: Primary CAM explains the erroneous predicted class.
annotation_unit_policy.wrong_case_secondary_cam: Secondary CAM targets the ground-truth class and is reviewed separately.

important_constraints: Grad-CAM++ is post-hoc explanatory evidence and does not prove causal clinical reasoning.
No lesion segmentation ground truth is available.
Semantic disease-region localization must be visually reviewed.
The XAI cohort was deterministically stratified and is not an unbiased population sample.
No semantic conclusion is produced before the annotation template is completed.
